definition: Auer deference, from Auer v. Robbins (1997) and Bowles v. Seminole Rock (1945), is judicial deference to an agency's reasonable reading of its own ambiguous regulation. Kisor v. Wilkie (2019) kept the doctrine but confined it: the regulation must be genuinely ambiguous after all the tools of interpretation are exhausted, and the agency's reading must be authoritative, expertise-based and a fair and considered judgment.
